newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Mixed Asia markets play mainly to domestic factors.
newsitem.headline: Mixed Asia markets play mainly to domestic factors.

text.p: Asian markets were a mixed bunch on Thursday, with centres largely trading on domestic factors in the absence of a clear overseas lead.

The bellwether Tokyo exchange gained 0.79 percent, although the move was mainly put down to futures activity. Hong Kong was hit by a temporary fall in the U.S dollar, but by the close it had managed to retrieve most falls to end off just 0.06 percent.
Foreign buying was noted in a number of centres, notably Jakarta and Singapore.

Tokyo stocks closed higher, buoyed by technical buying linked with futures trading. Brokers said that the market was off a temporary bottom, but investors were not confident of the market's energy amid a lack of buying factors.
The key Nikkei 225 average powered up 166.10 points or 0.79 percent to close at 21,322.85. Its December futures added 120 points to 21,320.
"The market is currently driven by supply and demand balance in the futures market," said Keiji Arai, strategist at Sanyo Securities Co Ltd.
Hong Kong stocks clawed back most of their morning losses but still ended a hair down on worries over U.S.interest rates and the weakness of U.S. dollar, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index closed down 7.35 points at 11,586.68. Turnover was HK$4.81 billion, a hefty drop from Wednesday's HK$6.07 billion.
"People were a little nervous today about the dollar," said Angus Shillington of Asia Equity. "The trade report affected the dollar which in turn hit the equity markets."
Market sentiment in Hong Kong remains optimistic if not all that active, brokers said.
Seoul stocks ended lower across the board led by falls of large-capitalised shares, brokers said.
The composite index fell 8.95 points, or 1.14 percent, to provisionally end at 773.15. Losers led gainers by 610 to 277.
The Australian share market rebounded in afternoon trade led by a charge from market heavyweights BHP and CRA.
The All Ordinaries index ended 12 points up at 2247.1.
Taiwan stocks closed higher and ended 36.57 points or 0.56 percent up at 6,535.59, while Manila shed 11.56 points to 3,237.03.
A spate of buying by European fund managers, notably in banking stocks, lifted Singapore's Straits Times index by 23.78 points, or 1.09 percent, to 2,206.09.
Thai stocks closed up, amid buying of finance stocks, and on talk the prime minister may change his finance minister if he survived an ongoing censure debate against him, brokers said.
The SET Index rose nearly 1.0 percent or 9.83 points to 1047.86 in thin dealings.
Jakarta share prices ended sharply up on the back of active foreign buying of various blue chips, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 5.87 points, or 1.05 percent, to close at 565.56 points.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) fell 61.30 points or 1.80 percent to a provisional 3352.71 points.
Hong Kong gold bullion was boosted by buying from the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) and ended at US$382.20/383.70 an ounce, against US$383.05/55 at its New York close.
Asian crude futures drifted back and by 0800 GMT November Brent crude traded on Simex (The Singapore International Monetary Exchange) was down 6 cents at $22.25.
The dollar recovered from a temporary fall below 109 yen. At 1115 GMT, the dollar was trading at 109.34/41 yen and 1.5090/97 marks, against 109.15/25 and 1.5090/00 at Wednesday's New York close. .
